scn.garage-1975.title: Garage startup (1975)
scn.garage-1975.desc: First CPU, first profit, first $5M. Recommended with the tutorial.
scn.garage-1975.briefing: 1975. You have a garage, a handful of engineers and $2.5M from the first investors. Ship your first CPU before July 1, 1976, turn a profit and save up $5M before January 1, 1978. This scenario is a tutorial: the in-game tips are on.
scn.garage-1975.g1: Ship the first CPU before July 1, 1976
scn.garage-1975.g2: Close a month with a profit
scn.pc-boom-1980.title: The PC boom (1980)
scn.pc-boom-1980.desc: Personal computers are heading for every office. Take the middle segment, find OEM customers and earn steadily.
scn.pc-boom-1980.briefing: 1980: personal computers are entering every office and their makers need affordable processors. Win 15% of the Mid Range segment, sign three OEM contracts and make a profit six months in a row before January 1, 1986.
scn.pc-boom-1980.g1: Mid Range segment share of 15% or more
scn.pc-boom-1980.g4: Low End segment share of 10% or more
scn.fabless-1985.title: Fabless (1985)
scn.fabless-1985.desc: Design processors without a fab of your own. Become a foundry customer and take 10% of the market. Building a fab is forbidden.
scn.fabless-1985.briefing: 1985. You design processors but own no fab: production is ordered from a foundry. Building lines of your own is forbidden and loses the scenario. Become a foundry customer, take 10% of the market and reach $300M revenue over a year before January 1, 1991.
scn.fabless-1985.g3: Revenue of $300M or more over 12 months
scn.fabless-1985.g4: Ship a CPU of 20 MHz or more
scn.comeback-1985.title: Second chance (1985)
scn.comeback-1985.desc: A $20M debt, lagging technology and expensive loans. Climb out of the hole and make the company profitable again.
scn.comeback-1985.briefing: 1985. The company is in debt: minus $20M, the technology is behind and the bank charges 50% more interest. Get out of debt, make a profit six months in a row before January 1, 1989 and never drop below −$80M.
scn.comeback-1985.g1: Get out of debt: money at zero or above
scn.foundry-1990.title: The foundry (1990)
scn.foundry-1990.desc: A big fab and an empty customer list. Find customers and turn capacity into revenue.
scn.foundry-1990.briefing: 1990. You have a big fab and no customers yet. Find three customers and earn $200M from them over a year before January 1, 1996.
scn.foundry-1990.g2: Customer revenue of $200M or more over 12 months
scn.mhz-race-1990.title: The 100 MHz race (1990)
scn.mhz-race-1990.desc: Who ships a 100 MHz CPU first? Losing the race loses the scenario.
scn.mhz-race-1990.briefing: 1990. Every company is rushing for the first 100 MHz. Ship such a CPU before your rivals do - losing the race means defeat. Then take 20% of the High End segment before January 1, 1996.
scn.mhz-race-1990.g1: Be first to ship a 100 MHz CPU
scn.mhz-race-1990.g2: High End segment share of 20% or more
scn.ghz-race-1995.title: The gigahertz race (1995)
scn.ghz-race-1995.desc: The race for a gigahertz. Ship a 1 GHz CPU first and hold the High End segment.
scn.ghz-race-1995.briefing: 1995. The race for a gigahertz. Ship the first 1 GHz CPU - if a rival gets there first, the scenario is lost. Then take 25% of the High End segment before January 1, 2003.
scn.ghz-race-1995.g1: Be first to ship a 1 GHz CPU
scn.ghz-race-1995.g2: High End segment share of 25% or more
scn.power-wall-2000.title: The power wall (2000)
scn.power-wall-2000.desc: Clock speeds hit the power limit. Build a multicore CPU under 65 W and win the industrial segment.
scn.power-wall-2000.briefing: 2000. Clock speeds are running into the power limit. Ship a multicore CPU of 2 GHz or more that draws up to 65 W, take 20% of the Industries segment and stay profitable for 12 months in a row before January 1, 2008.
scn.power-wall-2000.g1: Ship a CPU: 2+ cores, 2 GHz or more, up to 65 W
scn.power-wall-2000.g2: Industries segment share of 20% or more
scn.power-wall-2000.g4: High End segment share of 15% or more
chl.tight-credit.title: Tight credit
chl.tight-credit.desc: The credit limit is halved: your default threshold is computed from half the limit. +15% score.
chl.tight-credit.fail: There is no fail condition: the rule applies for the whole game.

chl.no-oem.title: No OEM
chl.no-oem.desc: Fail if you have any active OEM contract. Not available for a foundry. +20% score.

chl.fabless-purist.title: Fabless only
chl.fabless-purist.desc: Fail if you get fab lines. For a fabless company only. +20% score.
chl.no-debt.title: No debt
chl.no-debt.desc: Fail if cash stays below zero for over 30 days. +25% score.
